The Wedding

The Details

Everything you need to plan your Saturday. If something isn’t answered here, head to the FAQ or just text us.

Venue

Stonewall Hill Farm
412 Hubbell Hill Road
Roxbury, NY 12474

A restored 1880s dairy barn on 32 acres of meadow and second-growth forest in the western Catskills. The ceremony will be in the lower meadow (look for the chuppah of ferns); dinner and dancing happen in the barn. The farm is about a 5-minute drive from the village of Roxbury and roughly 3 hours northwest of NYC.

Parking & Arrival

There is on-site parking in the upper field — golf carts will shuttle anyone who doesn’t want to walk the (gentle) hill down. Please arrive between 1:15 and 1:45 PM so we can start the ceremony on time.

We’ll also run two shuttle vans from the Lazy Crow Inn and the Catskill Lodge starting at 1:00 PM, with return trips at 10:00, 11:00, and 11:30 PM. Details and pickup times will go out to RSVPed guests in early September.

Rideshare

Uber and Lyft do not reliably operate in this part of Delaware County, especially after 9 PM. Please plan to take the shuttle or arrange a ride in advance. Local cab options: Catskill Car Service (607-326-2240) and Roxbury Taxi (607-326-7700). Book ahead.

Weather

Mid-September in the Catskills is — knock on wood — usually gorgeous. Expect daytime highs around 70°F (21°C) and nighttime lows around 50°F (10°C). It can also rain sideways, so bring a layer. We have a full tent backup plan if the weather doesn’t cooperate; you’ll never be soaked at our wedding, we promise.

Accessibility

The ceremony site is on grass with a gentle downhill slope; we’ll have a small fleet of golf carts running constantly for anyone who would rather ride than walk. The barn has a ramp entrance and an accessible single-stall restroom.

If you have specific accessibility needs (mobility, hearing, sensory), please flag it on your RSVP and we’ll make sure you’re taken care of.

Kids

We love your kids. We are, with great love, having an adults-only celebration so that you can dance until midnight without worrying about anyone’s bedtime. The exceptions are nursing babies and the small handful of kids in the wedding party, who have been negotiated for individually.

A few of the nearby inns can recommend trusted local sitters — happy to connect you. Just ask.

Dress Code

Garden Formal

Think: the most beautiful version of an outdoor wedding on a working farm. Long sundresses, linen suits, midi skirts, florals, jumpsuits, suits in dusty colors. Anything you would wear to a really nice garden party. Bring a layer for when the sun goes down.

The ceremony and cocktail hour are on grass. Please, for your own ankles, leave the stilettos at home.

Block heels, flats, wedges Stilettos Linen, silk, cotton A tuxedo (unless you really want to) Florals, dusty pastels, sage, terracotta White, ivory, cream (that’s Maya’s job) A jacket or wrap for the evening Heavy fabrics that won’t breathe at 4pm
The Day

Schedule

Saturday, September 19, 2026

  1. 1:00 PM

    Shuttles depart from hotels

    Pickups at the Lazy Crow Inn (12:50 PM) and the Catskill Lodge (1:05 PM). The vans seat 14; we’ll run two rotations if needed. Try to be early.

    Hotel lobbies
  2. 2:00 PM

    Ceremony

    We get married! Outdoors in the lower meadow, about 30 minutes long, officiated by Maya’s aunt Lillian. There will be Sarah Vaughan, a poem by Ross Gay, and, statistically, at least one of us crying.

    Lower meadow
  3. 3:00 PM

    Cocktail hour

    Negronis, a smoky mezcal spritz called the “Hubbell Hill,” a thoughtful zero-proof menu, and passed hors d’oeuvres from the team at Phoenicia Diner. Live trio on the side porch.

    Barn porch & orchard
  4. 5:00 PM

    Dinner

    Long-table, family-style. Local farm vegetables, a wood-fired main, and a lot of bread. Toasts begin around 6:15. Vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options for everyone who told us in advance — please do.

    Inside the barn
  5. 8:00 PM

    Dancing

    The Brooklyn-based band Future Holiday plays a set of 70s soul, disco, and a few unhinged surprises, then DJ Margo takes over until close. Late-night snack drop around 10:30: little burgers, fries, a stack of cold watermelon.

    Barn floor
  6. 11:00 PM

    Shuttles back

    Last shuttle leaves at 11:30 PM sharp. Please don’t miss it — your phone will not get a Lyft in Roxbury at midnight. We will be sad if we don’t get to say goodbye, so come find us before you leave.

    Upper field

What to bring

  • A layer for after sunset (it gets cool, fast)
  • Cash for the late-night shuttle tip jar (optional but loved)
  • Shoes you can actually dance in
  • Your phone — but please put it down during the ceremony, we have a photographer
  • Tissues, if you’re a crier
  • An open heart and an empty stomach

What to leave at home

  • Anything white, ivory, or cream-colored
  • Stilettos (we mean it about the grass)
  • Wedding gifts — please send to the registry address, not the venue
  • Your camera flash during the ceremony
  • Stress about being late — but also, don’t be late

Photography

Our photographer is Imani Foster, who is wonderful, fast, and unobtrusive. During the ceremony we’re asking for an unplugged 30 minutes — phones away, just be with us. After the ceremony, photograph everything, tag us, share the link to the gallery we’ll send out.

Smoking

The barn and immediate grounds are non-smoking (it’s a working farm with a lot of hay). There’s a designated spot down by the orchard with a fire pit and an ashtray. We’ll signpost it.

RSVP — Due August 1
